scope: Portable CPU control-flow tests only; no model weights, native inference, GPU execution or runtime compilation. This does not revise historical PR14 evidence.

initial_broad_run.raw_log: work/portable-tests.log (left unchanged, outside this evidence note)

direct_call_check.result: The same three unmodified test functions called directly with pytest.MonkeyPatch and pytest.raises all pass.

cause.test_mock: checker.os is the shared os module; monkeypatch.setattr(checker.os, fstat, fail) therefore replaces os.fstat process-wide until fixture teardown.
cause.runner_behavior: Installed pytest 9.2.0 FDCapture.snap and FDCaptureBinary.snap call os.fstat(self.tmpfile.fileno()) to check for empty captured output. The snapshot occurs after the test call and before monkeypatch fixture teardown.
cause.effect: The application correctly raises and pytest.raises catches the injected exception. FD capture then reuses the still-patched os.fstat and raises the same exception again, producing a reported failure.
cause.classification: Pre-existing test-harness/environment compatibility issue, independently reproduced on unmodified PR14; not a GLM backend regression.

validated_workaround.comparison_note: The broader working tree had additional tests by this later run; totals must not be presented as the same fixed suite as the initial 585-pass run.

recommended_minimal_actions: Keep historical code and scientific evidence unchanged.
Use --capture=sys for this portable rerun, or align a new CI environment with its explicitly pinned validated pytest dependency.
If a future test-only fix is desired, scope the os.fstat patch with monkeypatch.context() around the tested call so it is restored before the test returns; no such code change was made here.
